---
title: "{{< fa list-check >}} Step 5: Test your setup"
---

[Due by **{{< var due.setup >}}**]{.highlight-yellow}

This is the same idea as the setup check in the first workshop: prove the whole chain works while there is still a week to fix it if it does not.

You will clone a repository, let the agent make one small change, and open an issue to report the result.

## {{< fa code-branch >}} 1. Clone the setup repository

You will receive an invitation to a repository named `setup-USERNAME` in the [{{< var course.code >}} organization]({{< var course.github-org >}}), where `USERNAME` is your GitHub handle. Accept the invitation, then clone the repository the way you did in the first workshop.

If cloning fails, that is a Git authentication problem rather than an agent problem. The [{{< var prerequisite.title >}} pre-work]({{< var prerequisite.site >}}) covers it, and your personal access token from July should still work.

## {{< fa terminal >}} 2. Start the agent

Open a terminal, move into the folder you just cloned, and start Claude Code:

```bash
cd setup-USERNAME
claude
```

The first run asks you to sign in. Use the account details from the email described in [Step 4](04-install-claude-code.qmd).

## {{< fa wand-magic-sparkles >}} 3. Give it one task

Type this, exactly as written, and press enter:

```
Read README.md, then add a line to it saying who you are and what
version you are. Commit the change with a clear message.
```

Watch what happens. The agent will ask permission before it writes the file and before it commits. [Say yes to both]{.highlight-yellow}.

Three things are worth noticing while it works, because they are the whole subject of the workshop:

- it read a file before changing it
- it asked before doing anything that changes something
- it wrote the commit message itself

## {{< fa arrow-up-from-bracket >}} 4. Push

In the same terminal:

```bash
git push
```

Then open your repository on GitHub and check that the commit is there.

## {{< fa circle-exclamation >}} 5. Report that you are done

On your `setup-USERNAME` repository, open an issue:

- **Title:** `Setup complete`
- **Body:** paste the output of `claude --version`, and say which operating system you are on
- **Assignee:** `{{< var github-handle >}}`

Same as the first workshop: the issue is how we know you are ready.

::: {.callout-important}
## If any part of this failed

Open the issue anyway. Title it `Setup problem`, say which of the five parts broke, and paste the error message. Assign it to `{{< var github-handle >}}`.

This is the point of having a due date a week out. A setup problem found on {{< var due.setup >}} is half an hour of work; the same problem found at 09:00 on the day costs you the morning.
:::
